facts.value: Contract law concerns enforceable promises, and can be summed up in the Latin phrase pacta sunt servanda (agreements must be kept).
facts.programme_association: Law - Masters or PhD | University of Limerick

facts.value: In common law jurisdictions, three key elements to the creation of a contract are necessary: offer and acceptance, consideration, and the intention to create legal relations.
facts.programme_association: Law - Masters or PhD | University of Limerick

facts.value: Consideration indicates the fact that all parties to a contract have exchanged something of value.
facts.programme_association: Law - Masters or PhD | University of Limerick

facts.value: Some common law systems, including Australia, are moving away from the requirement of consideration.
facts.programme_association: Law - Masters or PhD | University of Limerick

facts.value: The idea of estoppel or culpa in contrahendo can be used to create obligations during pre-contractual negotiations.
facts.programme_association: Law - Masters or PhD | University of Limerick

facts.value: Civil law jurisdictions treat contracts differently in several respects, with a more interventionist role for the state in both their formation and enforcement.
facts.programme_association: Law - Masters or PhD | University of Limerick

facts.value: Compared to common law jurisdictions, civil law systems incorporate more mandatory terms into contracts.
facts.programme_association: Law - Masters or PhD | University of Limerick

facts.value: Civil law jurisdictions allow greater latitude for courts to interpret and revise contract terms.
facts.programme_association: Law - Masters or PhD | University of Limerick

facts.value: Civil law jurisdictions impose a stronger duty of good faith.
facts.programme_association: Law - Masters or PhD | University of Limerick

facts.value: Civil law jurisdictions are more likely to enforce penalty clauses and specific performance of contracts.
facts.programme_association: Law - Masters or PhD | University of Limerick

facts.value: Civil law jurisdictions do not require consideration for a contract to be binding.
facts.programme_association: Law - Masters or PhD | University of Limerick

facts.value: In France, an ordinary contract is said to form based on a 'meeting of the minds' or a 'concurrence of wills'.
facts.programme_association: Law - Masters or PhD | University of Limerick

facts.value: Germany has a distinct approach to contracts that is closely tied to property law.
facts.programme_association: Law - Masters or PhD | University of Limerick

facts.value: Germany's 'abstraction principle' (Abstraktionsprinzip) means that the personal obligation of contract forms separately from the title of property being conferred.
facts.programme_association: Law - Masters or PhD | University of Limerick

facts.value: When contracts are invalidated for some reason, the contractual obligation to pay can be invalidated separately from the proprietary title of the car.
facts.programme_association: Law - Masters or PhD | University of Limerick

facts.value: Unjust enrichment law, rather than contract law, is then used to restore title to the rightful owner.
